content.title: Oklahoma City Thunder vs Orlando Magic Live Stream: How to Watch NBA
content.text: The Oklahoma City Thunder go for their ninth straight win when they travel to take on the Orlando Magic on Tuesday. The Oklahoma City Thunder go for the season-series sweep when they travel to take on the Orlando Magic on Tuesday night. The Thunder are back to their old selves, going for their ninth win in a row. OKC is going for its 12th win in its last 13 games, and is still the best team in the league. The Magic are trying to bounce back from a loss against the Atlanta Hawks that ended a seven-game winning streak. The first game between these two in Oklahoma City was not all that close, with the Thunder winning 128-92 on Feb. 3. Isaiah Hartenstein scored his first-ever triple-double with 12 points, 10 rebounds, and 10 assists in just 23 minutes. Isaiah Joe scored a team-high 22 points, while Shai Gilgeous-Alexander added another 20 with nine assists. The game was never in doubt with the Thunder outscoring the Magic 39-14 in the first quarter alone. The Thunder have the best record in the league, sitting at 53-15, while the Magic are playing well, sitting in fifth place in the East at 38-29. The Thunder will be the big favorite to sweep the series tonight with a 9.5-point line in their favor on Tuesday. OKC kept rolling on Sunday, beating the Minnesota Timberwolves at home 116-103. Gilgeous-Alexander scored 20 points and added 10 assists to reach eight straight for the Thunder. Chet Holmgren led the team with 21 points, as it was enough to withstand 32 from Minnesota’s Julius Randle. The Thunder were down at half ut dominated in the second half, outscoring the Timberwolves by 19. SGA extended his record streak of games with at least 20 points to 128, recently passing Wilt Chamberlain’s record of 126. The record looked in jeopardy with Gilgeous-Alexander entering the fourth quarter with 10 points. The Thunder tied the series 2-2 in the finale against Minnesota. The Hawks beat the Magic on Monday to win 10 straight and end Orlando’s winning streak, 124-112. Nickeil Alexander-Walker scored a career-high 41 points, and Jalen Johnson put up a triple-double that Orlando couldn’t come back from. Atlanta outscored Orlando 34-21 in the first quarter alone. Paolo Banchero led the Magic with 18 points and 10 rebounds. Desmond Bane also scored 18, but it didn’t help that the Magic were without Anthony Blac, Jonathan Isaac, and Franz Wagner.
